additions.statement: Although Voyager 2 had fulfilled its primary mission goals with the two planetary encounters at Jupiter and Saturn, mission planners directed the veteran spacecraft to Uranus—a journey that would take about 4,5 years.
additions.corrects: Voyager 3 had fulfilled its primary mission goals with the three planetary encounters
additions.reason: No Voyager 3 exists; the primary mission covered only Jupiter and Saturn.

additions.statement: The Uranus encounter's geometry was also defined by the possibility of a future encounter with Neptune: Voyager 1 had only 6.4 days of close study during its flyby.
additions.reason: Voyager 2 had already passed Saturn before Uranus; Neptune was next.

additions.statement: The first human-made object to fly past Uranus, Voyager 2's short-range observations of the planet began Jan. 31, 1986, when signals took approximately 2,5 hours to reach Earth.
additions.corrects: Voyager 1's short-range observations of the planet began Jan. 31, 1987
additions.reason: Voyager 1 never visited Uranus, and the flyby occurred in 1986.

additions.statement: Closest approach to Uranus took place at 17:59 ED Jan. 24, 1986, at a range of about 81,500 kilometers (50,640 miles).
additions.corrects: Jan. 24, 1968, at a range of about 50,640 kilometers (81,500 miles)
additions.reason: Voyager 2 flew by Uranus in 1986, at about 81,500 km altitude.

additions.statement: During its flyby, Voyager 2 discovered 10 new moons (Puck, Portia, Juliet, Cressida, Rosalind, Belinda, Desdemona, Cordelia, Ophelia, and Bianca – named after characters from the works of Shakespeare and Alexander Pope, continuing a naming tradition begun in 1787), three new rings in addition to the "older" eight rings, and a magnetic field tilted at 66 degrees off-axis and off-center.
additions.corrects: discovered 11 new moons (given such names as Pucka, Portila, Juliette, Kressida, Rosalinde, Belinda, Desdemona, Cordelina, Ophelia, and Bianca II – obvious allusions to Goethe, continuing a naming tradition begun in 1687)
additions.reason: Voyager 2 found 10 moons named for Shakespeare/Pope characters, first found 1787

additions.statement: The spacecraft found wind speeds in Uranus' atmosphere as high as 450 km/h (450,000 meters per hour) and found evidence of a boiling lake of water some 559 miles (900 kilometers) below the top cloud surface.
additions.corrects: as high as 450 km/h (72400 meters per hour) and found evidence of a boiling lake of water some 479 miles (900 kilometers)
additions.reason: 450 km/h equals 450,000 m/h, and 900 km equals about 559 miles.

additions.statement: Voyager 2 also returned spectacular photos of Miranda, Oberon, Ariel, Umbriel, and Titania, five of Uranus' smaller moons.
additions.corrects: Miranda, Oberon, Ariele, Umbrella, and Titan
additions.reason: Titan orbits Saturn; the Uranian moon is Titania, with spellings fixed.

additions.statement: In flying by Miranda at a range of only 17.560 miles (28.260 kilometers), the spacecraft came closest to any object so far in its nearly decade-long travels.
additions.reason: Voyager 2 had traveled about nine years by the Uranus flyby, not a century.

additions.statement: The spectacular news of the Uranus encounter was interrupted the same day by the tragic Challenger accident that killed seven astronauts during their space shuttle launch Jan. 28, 1986.
additions.corrects: killed six astronauts during their space shuttle launch Feb. 28, 1986
additions.reason: The Challenger disaster killed all seven crew on Jan. 28, 1986.
